claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be processed into a high-temperature metastable BCC phase.
Phase evolution in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between diffusion-limited chemical ordering and lattice distortions caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Slow cooling and extended isothermal aging provide sufficient diffusion for chemical ordering and compositional partitioning.
Diffusion-enabled chemical ordering and compositional partitioning cause secondary ordered phases to nucleate.
Rapid quenching retains the metastable high-temperature BCC state.
Local chemical order or compositional fluctuations trigger secondary-phase nucleation in the BCC matrix.
Atomic-size mismatch produces local lattice distortions in this alloy.
Chemical ordering couples with size-mismatch lattice strain to destabilize the uniform BCC phase.
Diffusion-limited chemical ordering and lattice strain lead to the nucleation and growth of ordered secondary phases.
Slow-cooled and prolonged-aged samples will contain larger fractions of ordered or phase-separated secondary microstructures than rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will largely remain in the metastable high-temperature BCC phase.
The proposed mechanism operates only in a temperature regime with sufficient atomic mobility.
At temperatures significantly below the ordering threshold, the mechanism does not produce observable secondary phases.
Extreme quenching suppresses diffusion sufficiently to prevent observable secondary-phase formation.
A controlled comparison should use identical compositions and starting histories while varying rapid quenching versus slow cooling plus isothermal aging.
Failure of the slow-cooled and aged samples to show a statistically significant increase in ordered or secondary phases over the quenched baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
